text:
If you’ve got outdoor plans, Tuesday is an easy one to use: a chilly 43-degree start gives way to full sunshine and a high right around 64. A north breeze at 5 to 9 mph will keep the day feeling crisp rather than warm, but with the lake staying relatively calm, broad-water waves a foot or less, it’s a fine day to be outside. Water temperatures are around 63, so take that chill seriously if you’re getting in.

Clear skies tonight will send temperatures back toward 44, and a touch of frost is possible in the colder spots. Wednesday stays sunny and nudges warmer, with a high near 67, though the models range from the mid 60s to the upper 60s, so don’t overplan around the exact number. Enjoy the sunshine today and tomorrow, but bring a layer for the morning and be off the water before the north wind picks up tonight.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Tuesday! It was cool again this morning with most places starting off in the 30s to lower 40s. We do have a bit more in terms of morning cloud cover to start the day, but we should lose that and pick up more sunshine by the time we head into this afternoon. Temperatures start to turn a bit warmer, as we head back into the low and mid 60s come this afternoon. Clear skies tonight will set us up for a cool and potentially frosty start to Wednesday. Most of us will see overnight lows that fall into the 30s and lower 40s to start Wednesday.
